thread:
Incident Bot: ALERT · Elevated 5xx + upstream timeouts for customer Larkspur on Dedicated cluster dkp-east-2. 1.8% 5xx over baseline, spike started ~15:02 UTC. Paging oncall. (alert_id: rbw-5xx-173890)
Devon (oncall): ack — I’m on it. Pulling metrics and checking recent deploys.
Alice (SRE): I see a KV eviction spike on dkp-east-2 around 15:01. Could be noisy tenant or memory pressure. Links: http://internal.metrics/dkp-east-2?range=30m
Bob (Runtime): Confirming increased request latency to public gateway for a subset of Larkspur routes: /gen and /chat. Error signature: upstream timeout (504) and rapid 5xx ramp.
Claire (Support): Jordan from Larkspur just flagged timeouts for their customers. They report increased error rate starting ~15:05. Jordan, any additional impact notes?
Jordan (Customer Ops): TL;DR — 10% of requests failing for some org IDs, mostly shorter prompt workloads. Customer is seeing degraded UX in their webapp. They’re starting a war room.
Devon (oncall): Next steps: 1) confirm noisy tenant vs infra; 2) if noisy tenant, isolate and throttle; 3) if infra, failover routing to fallback pool. Who can check per-tenant request distribution?
Bob (Runtime): Running query across gateway logs now. snippet:
```
# gateway query
select tenant, count(*) as errors from requests where status>=500 and cluster='dkp-east-2' and ts> '2026-03-15T15:00:00Z' group by tenant order by errors desc limit 20;
```
Bob (Runtime): results coming back — top offender: tenant=larkspur-prod (44% of 5xx), tenant=public-test (12%), rest <5%. So looks concentrated on Larkspur but not entirely isolated.
Alice (SRE): KV metrics: node pool mem_used spikes with many evictions; p99 eviction rate increased ~x10. Also see throttle logs from scheduling layer hitting eviction-protection. Possible model cache pressure due to sudden short-sequence heavy RPS.
Nate (Dedicated Eng): On dkp-east-2 I’m seeing GPU utilization within normal but host memory climbs on a subset of nodes (n-04,n-07). These machines host Larkspur dedicated slices. Might be Larkspur job hitting a memory leak or unbounded batching.
Devon (oncall): Can we temporarily move Larkspur to their dedicated spare capacity or route their traffic to dkp-east-3? What’s the impact/latency delta?
Nate (Dedicated Eng): dkp-east-3 has capacity but models are slightly older (quantized v2 vs v3). Latency delta ~+30ms median. Recommend staged migration: divert 20% traffic to dkp-east-3 and monitor error rate.
Bob (Runtime): I can add a route override for Larkspur -> fallback pool. Config snippet I’ll push:
```
# rollout
routes:
  - match: tenant=="larkspur-prod"
    weight: 80
    cluster: dkp-east-2
  - match: tenant=="larkspur-prod"
    weight: 20
    cluster: dkp-east-3
```
Devon (oncall): Do it. Also enable prefix/KV cache bypass for Larkspur for the short term (so we don’t thrash hot keys).
Bob (Runtime): Pushed 20% diversion at 15:18 UTC. Monitoring now.
Alice (SRE): After diversion, 5xx rate for Larkspur dropped from 1.8%->0.6% overall. Evictions still elevated on nodes but error tail reduced. (:+1: reaction by Devon)
Jordan (Customer Ops): Larkspur confirms errors down on their side, but some user sessions still show occasional timeouts. They appreciate the quick action.
Claire (Support): Noted customer gratitude, but they want root-cause timeline and ETA for full remediation.
Nate (Dedicated Eng): I’m SSH’ing into n-04 logs. Seeing repeated model cache reloads for certain short inputs — client pattern has many small concurrent requests causing KV thrash. I can limit per-tenant in-flight concurrency and add a small token-bucket throttle to smooth bursts.
Devon (oncall): Add a conservative throttle: global per-tenant concurrency cap 120 -> 60 for larkspur-prod, for next 30m, with auto rollback.
Bob (Runtime): Throttle config applied at 15:31 UTC. Early signal: requests/sec for larkspur down ~38%, 5xx rate now 0.2%. Latency slightly higher for some paths but within SLO.
Alice (SRE): Plan for next 2 hours: 1) keep diversion 20% and throttle in place; 2) collect heap profiles from model workers for n-04/n-07; 3) schedule deeper analysis on dedicated eng side. If heap growth persists, we may cordon nodes and shift remaining traffic.
Nate (Dedicated Eng): Starting heap profile collection (command: sudo /opt/profiler/collect --pid=nnn --duration=120s). Will upload artifacts to incident S3.
Jordan (Customer Ops): Sharing one of Larkspur's failing request traces — they send bursts of small chat messages (3-8 tokens) with no batching. They said they recently ramped traffic after a marketing push.
Devon (oncall): Action items and owners:
- Devon: Postmortem owner + customer comms + follow-up timeline.
- Nate: Investigate model worker memory usage and KV cache behavior (artifact: s3://incidents/1738901234/profiles).
- Alice: Monitor node-level evictions and prepare cordon play if needed.
- Bob: Keep routing throttle dashboard and rollback knobs handy.
- Claire/Jordan: Keep customer updated; ask Larkspur to stagger or enable client-side batching if possible.
Devon (oncall): Handoff — I need to go offline in 40m. If 5xx >1% again, escalate to PagerDuty high channel and ping @eng-runtime and @dedicated.
Bob (Runtime): Logging note: 15:18 apply diversion, 15:31 throttle applied. Current last_message_ts=1738904980.
Alice (SRE): Creating incident ticket INC-2026-173890 in tracker with initial impact and mitigation steps. Will attach logs and graphs.
Claire (Support): Documenting customer impact and sending interim message to Larkspur: "We've diverted some of your traffic and applied temporary throttles to reduce errors while our engineers investigate. We expect a full update within 2 hours."
Jordan (Customer Ops): Thanks team. Larkspur appreciated the transparency. They can hold on mass deployments for 2 hours while you investigate.
Nate (Dedicated Eng): Uploading heap dumps now. Early look shows frequent small allocations in tokenizer cache path; may be client pattern producing high churn.
Devon (oncall): Good work. Keep this thread updated. I'll compile the timeline for the postmortem and hand over to Alice for next shift. (note: leave channel open for followups)
Alice (SRE): I’ll take postmortem lead after Devon goes off-call. Leaving follow-up checklist in INC ticket. (:+1:)
Incident Bot: Incident resolved? evaluation: errors dropped to baseline 0.05% after throttles + diversion. Please mark status when stable.
Devon (oncall): Marking as mitigated; monitoring for 30m before close.
Bob (Runtime): Copy. Will keep a watch on alert channel and remove diversion only after heap profiles verified.
